dossier.purpose: codebase-memory-mcp is a single native C executable (stdio MCP server, one-shot CLI, installer, optional loopback graph UI) that indexes a repository with vendored tree-sitter grammars (162 grammar directories) plus in-process type resolvers branded 'Hybrid LSP' (10 language families) into a per-project SQLite knowledge graph. Coding agents query it through 17 MCP tools in code (README says 15): symbol search returning qualified name, file and line range; callers/callees tracing; read-only Cypher; code-snippet reads; git-diff impact mapping; architecture overview; index-coverage checks; ADR notes. It contains no LLM. It does not launch or talk to language servers (no LSP client code), exposes no tool that edits source files, and reports no compiler or language-server diagnostics. `install` writes MCP entries, skills, subagent definitions and context-only hooks into up to 45 agent clients, including Claude Code and Codex CLI.

claims.claim: 'The fastest and most efficient code intelligence engine for AI coding agents.' Full-indexes an average repository in milliseconds, the Linux kernel (28M LOC, 75K files) in 3 minutes; answers structural queries in under 1ms; ships as a native executable with a small verified runtime-asset set.

Tree-sitter AST analysis across all 162 languages, enhanced with Hybrid LSP semantic type resolution for Python, TypeScript/JavaScript/JSX/TSX, PHP, C#, Go, C, C++, Java, Kotlin, Rust and Perl; a persistent knowledge graph of functions, classes, call chains, HTTP routes and cross-service links; '15 MCP tools'; no language runtime, hosted service or API key.

Hybrid LSP is 'a lightweight C implementation of language type-resolution algorithms, structurally inspired by and compatible with major language servers' (tsserver/typescript-go, pyright, gopls, Roslyn, Eclipse JDT, rust-analyzer). 'No language server process, no per-project setup, no API key.' It refines CALLS and CALL_REFERENCE edges (ambiguous values stay USAGE) 'so the resulting graph mirrors what an IDE Go to Definition would resolve'.
Languages without a Hybrid LSP pass 'fall back to textual resolution, so you always get some answer'.
The project is a 'structural analysis backend'. It 'does not include an LLM' and relies on the MCP client to be the intelligence layer.

Tool tables list Indexing tools (index_repository, list_projects, delete_project, index_status) and Querying tools (search_graph, trace_path [alias trace_call_path], detect_changes, query_graph, get_graph_schema, get_code_snippet, get_architecture, search_code, manage_adr, ingest_traces). get_code_snippet: 'Read source code for a function by qualified name'. trace_path: BFS callers/callees, depth 1-5.

Edge types: CALLS; CALL_REFERENCE (a callable used at a supported reference site that resolves to one exact target); USAGE (identifier used but a unique callable target is not proven); IMPORTS, DEFINES, IMPLEMENTS, INHERITS and others.

Claude Code integration: detected automatically, MCP config in ~/.claude.json, 'Skill + three exact-tool graph agents; SessionStart, SubagentStart, non-blocking PreToolUse for Grep/Glob/Bash, and post-Read coverage'.

Installed hooks are 'fail-open and context-only'. PreToolUse observes Grep/Glob/Bash and injects matching graph symbols as additionalContext; PostToolUse on Read adds coverage context; 'It never denies or replaces the requested tool call'.

Codex CLI integration: detected, $CODEX_HOME/config.toml, managed AGENTS.md activation pointer, skill, three read-only agents, SessionStart + SubagentStart; Codex users must review and trust the installed hooks through /hooks.
`install` configures 45 client surfaces (39 detected automatically, 6 conditional or explicit) and never flips experimental feature flags, YOLO modes or global permission bypasses.

'runs 100% locally and collects no telemetry'; 'cbm makes no network request of its own accord — it does not check for new versions in the background, and nothing phones home'; updates run from the install script, not the binary.

Every release includes checksums.txt (SHA-256); release pipeline claims SLSA Level 3 provenance, Sigstore cosign keyless signatures, VirusTotal scanning and a CodeQL gate; Linux '-portable' archives are fully static builds.

Benchmarked on Apple M3 Pro: Linux kernel full index 3 min, Django ~6 s, Cypher <1 ms; five structural queries ~3,400 tokens vs ~412,000 file-by-file. 'Exact reproduction of the figures above requires the original inputs and raw artifacts.'

integrations.cli: Yes. `codebase-memory-mcp cli <tool> [--flags]` runs any MCP tool as a one-shot local command without the daemon (README.md:631-664; src/main.c:1077-1079). Other subcommands: install, uninstall, update (prints the install-script command), config, allow-root, hook-augment, daemon start|stop|status, --ui/--port, --tool-profile (src/main.c:1085-1099, 1244-1268, 2444-2476).
integrations.mcp: Yes. Stdio MCP server is the default mode (src/main.c:1076; manual config README.md:451-464). The tool registry defines 17 tools (src/mcp/mcp.c:465-751); README says 15. It also serves 2 prompts, explore_codebase and review_change_impact (mcp.c:1140-1172), and handles resources/list (mcp.c:17702). `--tool-profile=scout|analysis` restricts the surface to 8 or 13 tools (mcp.c:842-918). 12 tools carry readOnlyHint=true (get_file_outline is deliberately annotated non-read-only: mcp.c:772-790, tests/test_mcp.c:1400-1406). MCPB bundles and an MCP Registry entry are published (server.json; .github/workflows/release.yml:550-623).
integrations.sdk_or_api: No client SDK found; the npm, PyPI and Go packages are installers/launchers (pkg/npm/bin.js:1-4; pkg/go/cmd/codebase-memory-mcp/main.go:1-5). A loopback-only HTTP API exists on 127.0.0.1:9749 when the UI is enabled: POST /rpc, restricted to tools/call for list_projects, get_graph_schema and get_code_snippet (src/ui/http_server.c:1766-1782, 1965-1968), plus /api/layout, /api/index, /api/index-status, /api/adr and /api/processes (http_server.c:1971-2031). No auth token exists; Host and Origin checks only (http_server.c:1812-1824, 1922-1931).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Claude Code: `install` writes the MCP entry to ~/.claude.json, the skill ~/.claude/skills/codebase-memory/SKILL.md, and agents codebase-memory-scout, codebase-memory and codebase-memory-auditor (tools Read, Grep, Glob plus graph MCP tools, permissionMode: plan). It registers hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json: SessionStart (startup|resume|clear|compact), SubagentStart (*), PreToolUse (Grep|Glob|Bash) and PostToolUse (Read). All hooks are context-only and fail-open (src/cli/cli.c:8350-8483, 4431-4432, 5232-5254, 5823-5840, 6104-6119; src/cli/agent_profiles.c:149-165, 509-517; src/cli/hook_augment.c:1-17; README.md:493, 546-550). Codex CLI: managed [mcp_servers.codebase-memory-mcp] block in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml, a small AGENTS.md pointer, skill, three read-only agents, and SessionStart + SubagentStart hooks calling `codebase-memory-mcp hook-augment` (cli.c:3741-3793, 3948-3955, 8551-8565; README.md:494, 539-542, 552-555). Neither integration adds language-server navigation or post-edit diagnostics: no hook matches Edit/Write/MultiEdit (cli.c:4431-4432), and no Claude Code plugin or lspServers manifest was found in the repo.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, account or API key (README.md:19, 174, 302). Code agrees: src/ has no outbound socket code, only AF_UNIX daemon IPC (src/daemon/ipc.c:709, 724) and loopback TCP (src/main.c:2110, 2216; the UI server binds 127.0.0.1 in src/ui/httpd.c:229-250). `update` only prints the install-script command (src/cli/cli.c:13405-13489). The curl-based downloader/updater is compiled only under CBM_CLI_ENABLE_TEST_API (cli.c:7876-7929, 13128-13310), which CFLAGS_PROD does not define (Makefile.cbm:78-88). The daemon update-check has 'deliberately NO production provider' (src/daemon/application.c:67-80). Stale conflicting text: SECURITY.md:17-30 says an api.github.com update check runs after MCP initialize, and scripts/security-allowlist.txt:52,71 plus scripts/security-network.sh:80-90 still allow it. Network is needed only to install or update. install.sh downloads the archive and checksums.txt from GitHub Releases over HTTPS (install.sh:24-82, 184-243). The npm/PyPI/Go wrappers download from GitHub Releases at install or first run and check SHA-256 (pkg/npm/install.js:517-596; pkg/pypi/src/codebase_memory_mcp/_cli.py:277-312). scripts/setup.sh calls api.github.com for the latest tag (scripts/setup.sh:153). Local runtime services: a per-account coordination daemon on an owner-only AF_UNIX rendezvous under /tmp or /private/tmp (docs/CONFIGURATION.md:153); an optional UI at http://127.0.0.1:9749 that auto-enables on first run for UI builds when no config file exists (src/ui/config.c:125-127; docs/CONFIGURATION.md:138); subprocesses git (watcher, detect_changes) and sh/xargs/grep (search_code: src/mcp/mcp.c:12609-12640). Diagnostics are opt-in and local (CBM_DIAGNOSTICS, README.md:302-317). The CI egress test (scripts/security-network.sh:60-96, Linux only) inspects IPv4 connect() calls and passes HTTPS to any IP as 'REVIEW'.

code.architecture: Single-process C core with helper processes. src/main.c picks a role: MCP stdio client, one-shot CLI, hook client, per-account daemon, or supervised index worker. src/daemon/ is the shared coordination daemon: AF_UNIX IPC, session/job/watch registry, exact-build admission barrier. src/mcp/mcp.c is the JSON-RPC server and 17-tool registry; compact_out.c renders token-lean output; index_supervisor.c runs crash/hang-isolated index worker subprocesses. src/pipeline/ runs multi-pass indexing (structure, definitions, calls, usages, HTTP/route linking, config, tests, git history, complexity, cross-repo); lsp_resolve.h, lsp_surface.c and pass_lsp_cross.c apply Hybrid LSP call-edge overrides (confidence floor 0.6); artifact.c exports .codebase-memory/graph.db.zst. src/store/ is the SQLite graph store with FTS5 search and Louvain clustering, queried by src/cypher/ (read-only openCypher subset). Supporting modules: src/semantic/ and src/simhash/ (similarity edges), src/discover/ (gitignore/.cbmignore), src/watcher/ (git polling), src/traces/ (ingest_traces stub), src/ui/ plus graph-ui/ (embedded React/Three.js UI), src/cli/ (installer and 45-client config writers), src/foundation/ (portability, subprocess supervision, locks, memory). internal/cbm/ holds the tree-sitter extraction engine, 162 vendored grammars and 10 in-process type resolvers in internal/cbm/lsp/. vendored/ holds sqlite3, mimalloc, yyjson, xxhash, tre and the Nomic token-embedding table. pkg/ holds npm, PyPI, Go, Homebrew, Scoop, Winget, Chocolatey and AUR wrappers.
code.packaging_and_release: Release flow (.github/workflows/release.yml, manual workflow_dispatch, owner-only per MAINTAINERS.md:58): lint, tests, build, smoke + soak, draft GitHub release, verify, publish npm/PyPI/MCP Registry, un-draft. _build.yml builds 8 products: linux amd64/arm64 dynamic, linux amd64/arm64 static '-portable', darwin amd64/arm64, windows amd64/arm64. It uses `scripts/build.sh --with-ui`, derives stripped and unstripped candidates, VirusTotal-scans all 24, selects one per product, and packages byte-for-byte with scripts/package-release.sh (archive = executable, LICENSE, install script, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md: package-release.sh:38-40). Artifacts: *.tar.gz, *.zip, *.mcpb, release-candidates.tsv, virustotal-candidate-results.tsv, release-selection.tsv, checksums.txt, sbom.json, *.bundle (release.yml:275-284). Integrity steps: SHA-256 checksums.txt (release.yml:194-201); build-provenance attestations for candidates, selected containers and checksums.txt (_build.yml:98-106, 433-441; release.yml:211-214); SBOM attestation for tarballs (release.yml:227-234); keyless cosign sign-blob bundles for every artifact (release.yml:236-248); npm publish with --provenance (release.yml:483-491); PyPI via twine API token with a hash-pinned toolchain and no attestation step found (release.yml:499-525); MCP Registry via GitHub OIDC (release.yml:619-623). Package versions are synced at publish time (release.yml:450-460). Checked-in Homebrew (0.10.3), AUR (0.8.1) and Winget (0.8.1) manifests lag. Only workflow definitions were read; no release artifacts were opened.
code.tests_and_ci: Tests: custom C framework (tests/test_framework.h) run via scripts/test.sh (ASan+UBSan build, parallel/sharded harness; --tsan leg). tests/ has 123 .c files, 39 shell contract/guard scripts, 2 Python tests and 4 helper headers; tests/repro has about 86 files; graph-ui has 12 vitest files; wrappers have 3 npm, 1 PyPI and 2 Go test files. Static counts here: 141 suite declarations in tests/test_main.c and 7,756 TEST( definitions across 122 files, versus the README's '6,768 tests across 120 suites' (README.md:428; hard-coded badge README.md:6). Tests were not run. CI: 22 workflow files, actions pinned by SHA, Dependabot for github-actions only (.github/dependabot.yml:1-6). pr.yml (pull_request to main): _security.yml (allow-list audit, UI audit, vendored integrity, ScanCode license gate, CodeQL gate), _lint.yml (no-skips policy, cppcheck 2.20.0, clang-format-20, clang-tidy-21 memory analyzer), _test.yml (ubuntu x64/arm64, macos-14, macos-15-intel, windows; sharded), and product-code-gated smoke on ubuntu/macos-14/windows plus a ci-ok gate. codeql.yml (c-cpp, push and PR to main). scorecard.yml (weekly + push). dco.yml. dry-run.yml and release.yml (manual). nightly-soak.yml (weekly), smoke.yml, fast-repro.yml and bug-repro.yml (manual or qa/** branches). cache-warm.yml (nightly). Smoke runs security-strings, security-install, security-network (strace) and fuzz scripts (_smoke.yml:125-134). I did not verify any CI run results.

risks: Scope fit for language-server navigation: no LSP client or server integration, no symbol-level edit tool and no diagnostics. All 17 tools are indexing, query or ADR tools (src/mcp/mcp.c:465-751). 'Hybrid LSP' is in-process heuristic type resolution for 10 language families (internal/cbm/lsp/; src/pipeline/lsp_resolve.h:34-39). Claude Code hooks are context-only on Grep/Glob/Bash/Read, with no Edit/Write hook or diagnostics (src/cli/cli.c:4431-4432).

Definitions and references are graph-derived and approximate: USAGE edges mean a unique target is not proven (README.md:220); languages without a Hybrid LSP pass use textual resolution (README.md:824). The project's own benchmark scores Python/TypeScript/Go/Rust/Java at 87%, OCaml and Haskell below 75%, and notes function properties often null (docs/BENCHMARK.md:75-81, 906-917). search_code shells out to sh/xargs/grep (src/mcp/mcp.c:12609-12640).

Index staleness: get_code_snippet reads live files by stored line ranges with no content check (src/mcp/mcp.c:9661-9691, 11444-11453). The watcher polls git every 5 s + 1 s per 500 files, up to 60 s (src/watcher/watcher.h:5-8). Coverage and freshness are explicitly 'best-effort' (mcp.c:690-692).

Documentation and manifest drift at v0.11.0: README says 15 tools (code 17), 7/11-tool profiles (code 8/13), 158 vs 162 languages, and overstates ingest_traces. SECURITY.md:17-30 describes an update check the code removed (src/daemon/application.c:67-80) and lists only 0.10.x as supported (SECURITY.md:326-331). docs/BENCHMARK.md is v0.3.0. scripts/setup.sh still requires Go 1.23+ (setup.sh:47, 98). Checked-in manifests lag: Homebrew 0.10.3 (pkg/homebrew/Formula/codebase-memory-mcp.rb:4), AUR 0.8.1 (pkg/aur/PKGBUILD:3), Winget 0.8.1, npm/PyPI/server.json 0.10.8.

Maintenance concentration: every path is owned by one handle (@DeusData) and advisory reviewers are 'TBD' (.github/CODEOWNERS:11-12; MAINTAINERS.md:19-47). SECURITY.md:71-80 calls it a 'solo, volunteer-maintained project' with best-effort handling. Most behaviour sits in very large single files (src/mcp/mcp.c 18,154 lines; src/cli/cli.c 14,011 lines).

Install integrity and platform floor: install.sh checks SHA-256 against a checksums.txt fetched from the same GitHub release and does not itself verify cosign or attestations (install.sh:184-243). README also documents `scripts/setup.sh | bash`, which downloads the non-portable Linux archive with no checksum check (README.md:343; scripts/setup.sh:147-176). The standard Linux binary needs glibc >= 2.38 (install.sh:167-169; scripts/ci/check-glibc-compat.sh:4-8), yet the checked-in Homebrew formula and AUR PKGBUILD point at those non-portable archives (pkg/homebrew/Formula/codebase-memory-mcp.rb:18-26; pkg/aur/PKGBUILD:12-13). WSL2 is undocumented.

Local attack surface and config writes: install.sh runs `install -y --force` (install.sh:338-345), rewriting agent configs and hooks for up to 45 clients. Each Claude Code Grep/Glob/Bash/Read call can spawn `hook-augment` (5 s hook timeout, 2 s default in-process deadline, ~1.1 s CPU identity hash on non-no-op calls: src/cli/cli.c:4447; src/cli/hook_augment.c:65-91; src/main.c:2760-2766). A loopback UI server on 127.0.0.1:9749 auto-enables on first run for UI builds with no config file (src/ui/config.c:125-127; docs/CONFIGURATION.md:138). It has no auth token, only Host/Origin checks (src/ui/http_server.c:1812-1824, 1922-1931), serves get_code_snippet via /rpc (http_server.c:1766-1782) and can start indexing via /api/index. Indexing containment is a breadth denylist unless CBM_ALLOWED_ROOT or allow-root is set (docs/CONFIGURATION.md:196-212; src/foundation/workspace.h:68-78).

Licensing and supply chain: the project is MIT (LICENSE) but bundles ~160 third-party grammars (mostly MIT; CC0, Apache-2.0 and ISC exceptions), zstd under a dual license with BSD selected, and Apache-2.0 data derived from nomic-ai/nomic-embed-code (THIRD_PARTY.md:49-66, 107; vendored/nomic/NOTICE:1-17). One Microsoft ML engine flags some release binaries as Trojan:Script/Wacatac.B!ml, and release policy tolerates exactly one such detection (SECURITY.md:175-190, 265-270). The CI egress test passes HTTPS to any IP as 'REVIEW' and inspects only IPv4 connect() (scripts/security-network.sh:60-96), so 'no phone home' rests mainly on code review and allowlists.

checks.statement: Claude Code: install writes the MCP entry to ~/.claude.json, the skill, and 3 agents (codebase-memory-scout, codebase-memory, codebase-memory-auditor; Read, Grep, Glob plus graph tools; permissionMode: plan); hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json: SessionStart (startup|resume|clear|compact), SubagentStart (*), PreToolUse (Grep|Glob|Bash), PostToolUse (Read), all context-only and fail-open. Codex: managed [mcp_servers.codebase-memory-mcp] block in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml, AGENTS.md pointer, skill, 3 read-only agents, SessionStart + SubagentStart hooks via hook-augment. No Edit/Write/MultiEdit hook and no plugin or lspServers manifest.
checks.note: cli.c:8359, 8370 and 8372 plan the writes for skills/codebase-memory/SKILL.md, <user_root>/.claude.json and settings.json; :8474-8483 prints the four hook groups. cli.c:4429-4432 defines the matchers 'Grep|Glob|Bash' and 'Read' with the comment 'context-only and fail open'. :5232-5254 upserts PreToolUse/PostToolUse; :5794 with :5823-5840 registers SessionStart for startup/resume/clear/compact; :6104-6119 registers SubagentStart '*'. agent_profiles.c:150-154 has the three slugs; :511-515 writes 'tools: Read, Grep, Glob' and 'permissionMode: plan'. hook_augment.c:9-12: 'NEVER blocks a tool call'. A repo-wide search found no 'lspServers', 'MultiEdit', Edit/Write matcher or plugin.json. Nits: the installed Codex hook command is '<absolute binary path> hook-augment' (cli.c:3814-3821, 9519-9522); the literal 'codebase-memory-mcp hook-augment' at :3948-3955 is the public/test helper. checks.statement: Hybrid LSP 'compatible with major language servers' / 'mirrors what an IDE Go to Definition would resolve' / no language server process (README.md:804), rated partial: no LSP client or textDocument/* traffic; 10 in-process resolver families; call-edge overrides accepted only at confidence >= 0.6, otherwise registry/textual resolution; check-lsp-originality.sh calls it an original C implementation
checks.note: The README.md:804 quotes match. A repo-wide search for 'textDocument/' hits only comments (java_lsp.h:10, java_lsp.c:7, tests/test_java_lsp.c:5); java_lsp.h:11 reads '*without* shelling out to javac'. No string literal names clangd, pyright, gopls, rust-analyzer, tsserver or jdtls in src/ or internal/cbm/. internal/cbm/lsp/ holds exactly 10 *_lsp.c files (c, cs, go, java, kotlin, perl, php, py, rust, ts), and all of them populate resolved_calls. lsp_resolve.h:34-39 defines CBM_LSP_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR 0.6f with fallback to the registry; the floor is applied at lsp_resolve.h:397, 446, 715, 757 and pass_parallel.c:2622, 2661, 3307, 3332. The comment at :37-38 lists only Go, C/C++, Python and PHP and is out of date. The phrase 'original C implementation' is at check-lsp-originality.sh:5, one line before the cited range 6-9. 'Partial' is a fair rating.
